government.note: Presidential republic: the directly elected President (two-round system, five-year term) is head of state and of government and appoints the Council of Ministers. The 1960 constitution reserves the vice-presidency and 24 of the 80 seats of the House of Representatives for Turkish Cypriots; these have not been filled since the 1963-64 crisis, so the House has 56 sitting members. The Republic's government does not control the north of the island, where the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, recognised only by Turkey, exists.

title.en: President of the Republic of Cyprus

holders.note: Elected as an independent backed by DIKO, EDEK, DIPA and others.

offices.note: Dates from the Wikipedia article on the President of Cyprus (five-year term, renewable once consecutively, per its infobox).

source.title: Wikipedia: President of Cyprus (list of presidents, term)

system.note: Open-list PR in six district constituencies with a Hare quota; remaining seats go to lists above a national threshold (its level is not recorded here). 56 seats are elected by Greek Cypriots; the 24 Turkish Cypriot seats have been left unfilled since 1963-64 and are recorded as 'vacant'. The House cannot dismiss the President. seats_2000 is the result of the May 1996 election.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the May 1996 House of Representatives vote (shares computed from the vote counts): Democratic Rally 34.47% (Christian democratic and liberal-conservative), AKEL 33.00% (communist party, recorded as reformed_communist), DIKO 16.43% (centrist), EDEK 8.13% (social democrat), United Democrats 3.69% (liberal), New Horizons 1.71%, ADISOK 1.44% and the Ecological and Environmental Movement 1.00% (classifications of the small parties are gameplay judgements), others 0.13%.

claims.note: The Republic of Cyprus claims the whole island; the north is administered by the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, which only Turkey recognises.
